boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named GCSU places for studying, gathering, performances, recreation and connection, supported by current university pages.

cards.title: Front Campus
cards.subtitle: Historic central lawn at Georgia College & State University
cards.notes: Use the lawn as an outdoor meet-up or break spot, and watch the university calendar for convocations, concerts and other scheduled events.
cards.short_summary: A campus lawn used for leisure activities and major university gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU identifies Front Campus as a gathering space and says it hosts leisure activities, convocations, graduations and outdoor concerts.
cards.source_title: Our proud traditions | Georgia College & State University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; follow posted university event and access guidance.

cards.title: The Bobcat Head
cards.subtitle: Front Campus crossroads
cards.notes: Make this marble mascot marker a group-photo stop while crossing Front Campus; respect the university’s documented graduation-related tradition around it.
cards.short_summary: A marble mascot depiction and recognized spot for group pictures.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU describes the Bobcat Head as a marble depiction of its mascot at the Front Campus crossroads and a popular place for group pictures.
cards.source_title: Our proud traditions | Georgia College & State University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor marker on Front Campus; do not chalk, paint or write on or near it.

cards.title: Ina Dillard Russell Library
cards.subtitle: Main campus library
cards.notes: Start research here by reserving a study room, arranging a research consultation or checking out technology through the library’s listed services.
cards.short_summary: The campus library combines research help, study-room reservations and technology checkout.
cards.evidence_claim: Russell Library lists research consultations, technology checkout and study room reservations among services for the campus community.
cards.source_title: Ina Dillard Russell Library | Georgia College & State University
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours and reservation requirements before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Russell Library Second Floor Computing Area
cards.title: Russell Library Second Floor Computing Area
cards.subtitle: Ina Dillard Russell Library
cards.notes: Use this named computing area when a campus desktop is more useful than a laptop; it provides both Windows and Mac workstations.
cards.short_summary: A library computer area with Windows and Mac stations.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU IT lists 47 Windows seats and four Mac OS seats in the Russell Library Second Floor Computing Area.
cards.source_title: Student Technology Resources | Georgia College & State University
cards.access_notes: Availability depends on open seats and library access; follow library computer-use rules.

cards.title: Russell Library First Floor Atrium
cards.subtitle: Ina Dillard Russell Library
cards.notes: Choose the atrium for a quick campus-computer session near the library entrance; GCSU lists six Windows seats in this specific area.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor library work area with six listed Windows computer seats.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU IT identifies the Russell Library First Floor Atrium as a Windows computer resource with six seats.
cards.source_title: Student Technology Resources | Georgia College & State University
cards.access_notes: Availability depends on open seats and library access; follow library computer-use rules.

cards.title: Blackbridge Hall
cards.subtitle: 111 S Clarke St., Milledgeville
cards.notes: Visit the Office of Community Engagement and Belonging here to ask about volunteer opportunities, service-learning resources and belonging programs.
cards.short_summary: A heart-of-campus home for community-engagement and student-belonging resources.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU says its Office of Community Engagement and Belonging is located in Blackbridge Hall and connects students with partnerships and programs.
cards.source_title: Office of Community Engagement & Belonging | Georgia College & State University
cards.access_notes: Contact the office for program details and availability.

cards.title: Wellness and Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 134 West Campus Drive
cards.notes: Use the WRC for fitness, free-play sports, wellness programs and organized recreation; bring your Bobcat ID and confirm eligibility before entry.
cards.short_summary: A West Campus recreation hub with fitness, sports and wellness programming.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU describes the WRC as a West Campus hub offering fitness, organized intramural and club sports, free-play sports and wellness options.
cards.source_title: Wellness & Recreation | Georgia College & State University
cards.access_notes: Controlled access; current enrolled students who pay applicable building and health fees may use the facility.

cards.title: Rec Fields
cards.subtitle: Behind the Wellness and Recreation Center, West Campus
cards.notes: Look for intramural or club-sport schedules that use these fields, then join a team or watch a tournament through the appropriate program.
cards.short_summary: A 10.5-acre field complex used for games and tournaments.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU says the Rec Fields sit on 10.5 acres behind the WRC and host an array of games and tournaments.
cards.source_title: Intramurals - Recreational Sports | Georgia College & State University
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to recreational-sports scheduling and facility rules.

cards.title: Russell Auditorium
cards.subtitle: Georgia College campus
cards.notes: Check Theatre and Dance announcements for productions and performances in this historic auditorium, then confirm ticketing or reservation details before attending.
cards.short_summary: The university’s principal performance space for music and theatre productions.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU identifies Russell Auditorium as the main performance space for music and theatre productions.
cards.source_title: Production Facilities - Theatre & Dance | Georgia College & State University
cards.access_notes: Access is event-dependent; check the department’s current production and ticket information.

cards.title: Campus Black Box Theatre
cards.subtitle: Campus Theatre, 137 W. Hancock St., downtown Milledgeville
cards.notes: See the current Theatre and Dance season for performances in this flexible-seating venue, and use the department’s ticket link for attendance details.
cards.short_summary: A downtown black-box venue for theatre performance, rehearsal and classroom work.
cards.evidence_claim: GCSU says the Campus Theatre includes a black box theatre with flexible seating, rehearsal and classroom space for its theatre department.
cards.source_title: Production Facilities - Theatre & Dance | Georgia College & State University
cards.access_notes: Access is event-dependent; Campus Theatre is at 137 W. Hancock St. in historic downtown Milledgeville.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Georgia College traditions, from a graduation superstition to annual campus rituals.

cards.title: Avoid the Bobcat Head
cards.subtitle: Front Campus graduation superstition
cards.notes: Find the marble Bobcat Head at Front Campus’s crossroads, take a group photo nearby, and leave its surface alone until your degree is complete.
cards.short_summary: A marble mascot marker with a pre-graduation superstition.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia College’s Blue Book says students should not step on the Bobcat Head before earning their degree or they will not graduate on time.
cards.source_title: The Georgia College Blue Book: The Traditions and Key Experiences of the Bobcat Nation
cards.access_notes: Outdoor Front Campus landmark; observe the superstition respectfully.

cards.title: Take the Green Towel on the Prowl
cards.subtitle: Bobcat spirit-towel tradition
cards.notes: Use the Green Towel at a spirited university event or photograph it while traveling, then share the image through the university’s stated submission route.
cards.short_summary: A portable green towel used to show Georgia College connection beyond campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Book identifies the Green Towel as both a spirit towel and a traveling towel for Georgia College community members.
cards.source_title: The Georgia College Blue Book: The Traditions and Key Experiences of the Bobcat Nation
cards.access_notes: Bring a towel only if one is provided or obtained through an approved university channel.

cards.title: Wear Blue and Green on Friday
cards.subtitle: Weekly Bobcat-color ritual
cards.notes: Wear Georgia College blue and green on Friday and keep an eye out for Thunder, whose appearance is part of the documented campus tradition.
cards.short_summary: A weekly color-wearing tradition tied to the Bobcat mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Book directs community members to wear blue and green every Friday and notes that Thunder may offer a special thank-you.
cards.source_title: The Georgia College Blue Book: The Traditions and Key Experiences of the Bobcat Nation
cards.access_notes: Wear school colors; mascot appearances vary by event.

cards.entity_name: Georgia College Alma Mater and Carillon
cards.title: Listen for the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: Campus carillon tradition
cards.notes: Pause when the carillon plays the Alma Mater and listen from campus; save the official sheet music if you want to follow the composition.
cards.short_summary: The school song is played by campus chimes on a weekday schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Book says the Alma Mater, composed in 1965, is played on the university carillon on weekdays.
cards.source_title: The Georgia College Blue Book: The Traditions and Key Experiences of the Bobcat Nation
cards.access_notes: Carillon timing may change; consult current campus communications before planning around a specific time.

cards.title: Receive the Class Pin at Convocation
cards.subtitle: New-student induction ceremony
cards.notes: If you are an entering student, attend Convocation, receive your class pin, and treat it as the formal marker of joining the Georgia College community.
cards.short_summary: New students receive a class pin during their official induction.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Book describes Convocation as students’ official induction and says new students receive a class pin.
cards.source_title: The Georgia College Blue Book: The Traditions and Key Experiences of the Bobcat Nation
cards.access_notes: Participation is associated with entering students; confirm current new-student programming.

cards.title: Form Your Class Year on Front Lawn
cards.subtitle: Weekend of Welcome class-photo tradition
cards.notes: During Weekend of Welcome, join your entering class on Front Lawn to form the digits of the class year for the elevated group photograph.
cards.short_summary: Each entering class forms its year numerals on the lawn for a commemorative photo.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Book says each entering class forms the digits of its class year on the front lawn during Weekend of Welcome.
cards.source_title: The Georgia College Blue Book: The Traditions and Key Experiences of the Bobcat Nation
cards.access_notes: For entering students during Weekend of Welcome; follow event staff directions.

cards.title: Bag Potatoes for Local Distribution
cards.subtitle: Annual fall service activity
cards.notes: Register through the GIVE Center when the fall Potato Drop is announced, then help bag donated potatoes for distribution to local community organizations.
cards.short_summary: A large annual volunteer effort that redirects potatoes to local recipients.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Book identifies Potato Drop as an annual fall signature service activity, with volunteers bagging potatoes for local organizations.
cards.source_title: The Georgia College Blue Book: The Traditions and Key Experiences of the Bobcat Nation
cards.access_notes: Annual scheduling and volunteer registration should be confirmed with the GIVE Center.

cards.title: Watch Front Campus Light Up
cards.subtitle: Pre-exam holiday-lighting tradition
cards.notes: Join the Front Lawn gathering before fall exams to watch the named historic halls light up, and enjoy the holiday music and refreshments if offered.
cards.short_summary: A Student Government Association holiday lighting of Front Campus halls.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Book says the Student Government Association invites campus to Front Lawn for the pre-exam lighting of five halls.
cards.source_title: The Georgia College Blue Book: The Traditions and Key Experiences of the Bobcat Nation
cards.access_notes: Annual pre-exam event; verify current date and weather plans with Student Government Association.

cards.title: See Greek Weekend Competition
cards.subtitle: Annual Fraternity and Sorority Life event
cards.notes: Attend publicly available Greek Weekend programming to watch chapter competitions such as the Step/Stroll Show and Greek Sing, following event guidance.
cards.short_summary: Chapters compete and celebrate academic and philanthropic work in an annual April program.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Book describes Greek Weekend as an annual April Georgia College Fraternity and Sorority Life event with chapter competitions.
cards.source_title: The Georgia College Blue Book: The Traditions and Key Experiences of the Bobcat Nation
cards.access_notes: Audience access and schedule vary; check current Fraternity and Sorority Life announcements.

cards.title: Celebrate at Lavender Graduation
cards.subtitle: Annual LGBTQ+ graduating-student recognition
cards.notes: If eligible, connect with the appropriate campus office about Lavender Graduation; allies can support participating graduates according to the current event guidance.
cards.short_summary: An annual recognition celebrating graduating LGBTQ+ students and allies.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Book says Lavender Graduation is held annually for graduating LGBTQ+ students and allies and first occurred at Georgia College in 2012.
cards.source_title: The Georgia College Blue Book: The Traditions and Key Experiences of the Bobcat Nation
cards.access_notes: Confirm current eligibility, registration, and guest arrangements with the organizing campus office.
